programme: No single recognizable complex or pathway unites the recurring factors. DLX5 and NKX3-2 share a genuine osteochondrogenic BMP-RUNX2 signature (targets include RUNX2, BMP4, COL10A1, SPP1, ALPL, GDF5), but the next most-recurring factors sit in entirely separate programmes: HOXC9 (posterior HOX/endothelial: CXCL8, STAB2), ZBTB4 (p53-CDKN1A chromatin repression: CDKN1A, SIN3A), BCL11A (hematopoietic globin-switching: HBB, HBZ, HBD), TCF3 (pro-B/T E2A circuitry: PAX5, EBF1, CD79A/B), SNAI1 (EMT: CDH1, VIM, ZEB1), GLI1 (Hedgehog-Wnt crosstalk: DKK2/3/4, SFRP1, and a documented ANO1 link), and CUX1/HOPX/MSC each standing alone. These are at least five non-overlapping regulatory programmes, not one module a biologist could act on as a unit.
role_in_a: Not applicable to a single programme. The record shows zero Open Targets or literature association for any of the twelve factors in Cardiovascular_Disease, so there is nothing here placing this list, or any subset of it, in disease A.
role_in_b: Not applicable to a single programme. Only GLI1 has a genuine documented tie to gut physiology relevant to IBS (Hedgehog-mediated repression of ANO1, a channel central to interstitial-cell-of-Cajal pacemaker activity and gut motility). The apparent MSC 'support' is very likely a gene-symbol collision between musculin (MSC, whose actual targets are FOXP3, IL10, IL2RA, CTLA4, IFNG) and the unrelated common abbreviation for mesenchymal stem cells, which is what the four retrieved papers are actually about.
shared_axis: No defensible shared mechanism is supported by this factor set. The recurring factors sort into unrelated regulatory programmes, and the two pieces of retrieved evidence (GLI1-ANO1, MSC-labelled papers) do not connect to each other or to the more strongly recurring HOXC9/ZBTB4/BCL11A, so there is no single axis that would explain why these two diseases would share it.
reasoning: A real module should be visible in the highest-recurring factors, but DLX5 (31/32) pairs mechanistically only with NKX3-2 (16/32, bottom tier), while HOXC9 (23/32), ZBTB4 (22/32) and BCL11A (20/32) — all more recurrent than NKX3-2/GLI1/HOXA11 — belong to lineages that share no targets with the osteochondrogenic or Hedgehog signatures. Essentially nothing in the record places any factor in Cardiovascular_Disease, and the sole recurring IBS-relevant signal beyond GLI1 (MSC) is best explained as a retrieval artifact rather than transcription-factor biology. Per the instruction to call a pair incoherent rather than force a story onto factors that merely co-occur, that is the honest read here.
support: PMID 30802137 — shows Gli proteins directly repress ANO1 transcription, a genuine and specific link between GLI1 and gut motility/ICC biology relevant to IBS, but this single link does not connect to any other factor in the list. PMID 41480397, 40691643, 40149563, 40740529 — retrieved under the MSC target-set match but all describe mesenchymal stem cell therapy/biology, not the musculin (MSC) transcription factor's own target programme; most likely a gene-symbol/abbreviation collision rather than real evidence for the factor MSC in IBS.
how_to_falsify: Take matched single-cell or spatial transcriptomic data from vascular tissue (CVD) and colonic mucosa/stroma (IBS) and test whether DLX5, NKX3-2, HOXA11, GLI1, HOXC9, ZBTB4, BCL11A, TCF3, SNAI1, CUX1, HOPX and MSC co-express within a shared cell population in both tissues, with correlated or co-accessible target-gene modules. If a common cell type and jointly regulated module emerges, the incoherent call is wrong and the true programme should be re-derived from that overlap. Separately, re-run literature retrieval restricted to 'musculin' or 'BHLHA20' plus its actual targets (FOXP3, IL10, CTLA4) to check whether the four MSC-labelled papers are a symbol collision or genuine — if real musculin papers discussing IBS turn up, the support assessment for that factor should be revised.
caveats: Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 32 patient-group comparisons, so 'concordant in N/32' reflects limited independent replication, not N separate studies. Open Targets records no Cardiovascular_Disease association for any of the twelve factors, and no IBS association except GLI1 at a low percentile (0.1785 of 2050 scored genes). RUNX2, which would mechanistically complete the DLX5/NKX3-2 osteochondrogenic story, was removed as tissue-generic to blood/colorectal tissue and also failed to generalize beyond single patient groups — its absence here is an artifact of the exclusion filters, not a missing piece to add back in. The single-view exclusions (IRF1, STAT2, ETS1, RUNX2, etc.) show several plausible immune/vascular regulators were tried and did not recur, reinforcing that this pairing's signal is thin rather than under-explored.
